attempt: test whether Silk damping can explain the BAO wiggle amplitude excess
the_contradiction_this_resolves: Two earlier readings disagreed. The kappa perturbation experiment said +-2% opacity moves the BAO peak by only 0.039pp, while the residual decomposition said the wiggle is 1.4% too strong with the excess growing with k - which is the signature of damping. This experiment settles it.
method: scale kappa by S in PerturbationBatch.coefficients and scale tc_epsilon by 1/S, so that the tight-coupling switch tcu = kappa > k/tc_epsilon fires at exactly the same time and only the damping changes. Measured the P(k=0.17)/P_CAMB ratio at z=0 for S = 2.00, 1.20, 1.00, 0.80, 0.50.

sensitivity.local: between S=0.80 and S=1.20, ln(1.2/0.8) = 0.405 and the ratio falls by 0.00801, i.e. -1.93% per unit ln kappa
sensitivity.cross_check_against_the_earlier_experime: the earlier reading was that +-2% kappa moves the peak by 0.039pp. ln(1.02) * 1.93% = 0.038pp. THE TWO AGREE TO TWO SIGNIFICANT FIGURES.
sensitivity.non_linearity: S=0.50 breaks the local trend (+7.715% against -1.93% per ln kappa predicting +1.34%), which is expected: halving the opacity is far outside the linear regime for damping.

verdict: SILK DAMPING IS REFUTED as the explanation for the wiggle excess.
the_arithmetic_that_refutes_it: to remove the 2.49% excess at the BAO peak the damping would have to be strengthened by 2.49/1.93 = 1.29 in ln kappa, i.e. opacity multiplied by 3.6. That is not a small correction to a recombination history; it would wreck the damping tail everywhere else and would have shown up long ago in the high-k ratios, which sit at +0.57..0.77%.
what_was_actually_wrong: not the kappa measurement - that was right all along - but the INFERENCE drawn from it in residual_decomposition.json. An amplitude excess that grows with k is consistent with weak damping, but consistency is not causation, and the sensitivity is two orders of magnitude too small to carry it.
consequence_for_the_decomposition: component 2 (the ~1.4% BAO wiggle excess) survives as a measurement but loses its proposed cause. It is now an unexplained amplitude defect with a known shape and no known mechanism.

what_is_still_standing.smooth_tilt: +1.25..1.50% low k easing to +0.57..0.85% high k, unexplained
what_is_still_standing.bao_wiggle_excess: about 1.4%, growing slightly with k, mechanism unknown

no_code_changed: the kappa scaling was done by monkeypatching inside the diagnostic only; nothing in the repository was modified.
patterns_worth_noting: this is the fifth hypothesis from the acoustic sector to fail (second-order TC exit values, tc_epsilon, baryon lag, cs2, and now Silk damping). The acoustic amplitude defect is real and reproducible but is not being produced by anything that has been varied so far.
